title: Show upload activity, peer counts and explicit torrent transfer states
description:
Fork research: parallel GPT-6 Astra source reviews, 2026-10-25. Current application baseline: 3ae404b.

## Purpose and evidence

Simple Torrent exposes upload/download rates, peers and ratio. Current Torrent model exposes verified downloaded content and download rate only, leaving seeding and stalled-download diagnosis unclear. Expose concise user-facing telemetry rather than raw upstream debug state.

## Acceptance criteria

- Add generated typed summary fields for upload rate/counters, useful download-transfer counters, active/known peer counts and queued/downloading/seeding/paused/stopped-by-policy state.
- Distinguish bytes transferred over the network from verified content on disk; reuse seeding accounting and document restart scope. Guard zero elapsed times/denominators and prevent negative, NaN or infinite displayed values.
- Sync only the minimal summary: no peer IPs, private tracker/passkey URLs, full upstream stats object or raw metainfo. Keep updates efficient and the mobile UI readable.
- Use local-peer fixtures to verify upload/download/idle/paused states, finite rates and accounting consistency, and browser checks for desktop/mobile display.

## Sources

- https://github.com/boypt/simple-torrent/blob/6f4942933b71106bae00b4f4c94438e3b315fca2/static/files/template/torrents.html#L39-L66

- https://github.com/jpillora/cloud-torrent/blob/3ae404b282d7678f90e16b0bf84a52d872fc73d9/frontend/src/components/TorrentItem.vue

## Scope

Implement within the existing Go engine, typed API, generated frontend models and authenticated handler chain. Use isolated legal fixtures; never test against live downloads. This is a new backlog item, not a claim that the proposed behavior already exists.

## Prerequisites

#78, #79.
